summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 15, part 115) in which Emma and Ray dine at an Italian restaurant run by the exuberant Gino. Emma admits she feels sheltered and unsophisticated, having lived most of her life on a frontier colony, and suggests Amah is more Whiston than the Whiston family itself. The passage also sketches the family history of Amah's clan, which began when a great-great-grandfather rescued them from a plague-stricken Polynesian island, and it introduces Grandfather Elliot George's sale of his Old Boston holdings to buy a majority share in a company.
one_line: Emma and Ray dine at Gino's restaurant, where Emma reveals her sheltered past and the long Whiston family history tied to Amah's clan.
key_facts: Emma tells Ray she has been very sheltered and that most of her life was spent on a frontier colony with fewer than a million people.
Emma says she is not sophisticated and has not traveled.
Ray jokes that he snores, his feet smell bad, he sleeps with his socks on, and he wears the same skivvies two or three days in a row.
Ray says Amah's reception of him explains her fear that he will try to steal Emma away.
Emma says Amah is more Whiston than she is, or than any of the family is.
Emma says Amah has held the family together for years, longer than Emma has been alive.
Amah's family has been with the Whiston family since the beginning, when a great-great-grandfather rescued them from a plague-stricken Polynesian island.
Gino is described as dark, burly, and bona fide Italian, a jovial and high-pressure restaurant host.
Gino recommends linguini al sugo di pescatore and Sicilian mostacciolo.
Emma puts her hand to her face after saying she sounds mercenary, and Ray uncovers her eyes.
Ray says the other night Emma said he was out of her league, and Emma replies that he is wrong about that.
Emma says she is uncomfortable discussing the family, Frederick, and anything Whiston, and avoids Ray's gaze when she does.
Grandfather Elliot George sells everything he owns in Old Boston to purchase a majority share in a company.
Ray senses Emma has been waiting a very long time to tell someone about the family.
Ray says he is not ready to call the relationship a success, saying it is too early to call it.
